independence_evidence: The about page says TNQ registered as a non-profit in 2003 and describes itself as a Canadian literary magazine based in Waterloo, Ontario, with its own board and volunteers; no media-group ownership.
qualifies_reason: Non-profit Canadian literary quarterly with four print issues a year, Issue 179 (Summer 2026) sold in its own shop and Issue 180 contents published in November 2026.
what_it_is: A Canadian literary quarterly publishing new fiction, poetry, personal essays and author interviews, with each issue loosely themed and including the results of its annual fiction, essay and occasional-verse contests. Issues are perfect-bound and sold singly or by subscription, alongside a digital edition and an online archive. It is aimed at readers and writers of contemporary Canadian literature.
uncertainties: Issue 180 has a full contents page on the site and its pieces went online on 2026-11-17, but it is not yet listed in the shop and no cover image for it was found, so the date is approximate (the previous issue, 179, is labelled Summer 2026 and was listed 2026-07-16). The only cover available is for Issue 179 (https://tnq.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/00745D_TNQ179-COVER_00.png, 1000 x 1071 px, publisher), which is not recorded as a candidate because it is not the most recent issue. Cover price is taken from the Issue 179 shop listing ($20 CAD; issues 177 and 178 were $15). Trim size and page count are not stated. The /issues/ index returned 403 to the fetcher.
